hints.title: Node Revisit Obstacle
hints.text: Standard graph searches prevent cycles by marking nodes visited, but visiting every node along a shortest route may require walking across an already visited node to reach unexplored branches. How can you define your search state so that revisiting a node with newly seen nodes counts as progress?

hints.title: State Bitmask Representation
hints.text: Represent each search state as a pair containing the current node index and an integer bitmask recording the subset of visited vertices, searching with breadth-first search across the state graph.

hints.title: Multi-Source Queue Traversal
hints.text: Initialize a queue with states (i, 1 << i, 0) for each node i from 0 to n - 1, along with a visited set. In each step, dequeue the front state. If its mask equals (1 << n) - 1, return the distance. Otherwise, for each neighbor, compute the new mask and enqueue it if unseen in the visited set.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

complexity.notes: Breadth-first search on state graph (current_node, visited_bitmask).
